motivation: R10AG alternated 110 loaded-rise plans and 490 load-seeking plans within its 600-command raise phase. The AH monotone center-first models stall even with perfect tracking. Test whether a single geometry plan can combine body-rise progress and restoration of weak distal load without serially suspending rise whenever one foot falls below the unchanged threshold.
scope: Exact s169 mathematical joint-reference kernel only. No native source ownership or task acceptance authority; future integration must validate native collection, controller ownership, energy, phase and report provenance.

phase_behavior.establish_distal_support: Return the unchanged V23 load-seeking or qualified measured-hold reference.
phase_behavior.raise_body: Search the original 135 body-pose candidates while lowering every weak-foot mathematical endpoint by the original load deficit rule. All-four qualification is not required for proposing a rise target; the original task still decides support, safety and success. If no feasible cost-decreasing pose exists, use the unchanged V23 reference as an explicit fallback.
phase_behavior.other: Refuse; future composition must dispatch the original stance and terminal behavior.

weak_load_rule: distance = 0.1 * dt * scale; deficit = clamp((0.019293 - qualified_native_impulse)/0.019293, 0, 1); lower the modeled foot endpoint by distance * deficit even when it is below the inferred plane. Missing presence, support or ordinary-unilateral flags imply zero qualified load. This is a joint-target planning rule, not an applied native contact force.
